Independent exact cofactor checks: (3,4) gives ratios 1,13/27,73/243,79/243 for the four classes and total 12297692033065156608; (4,3) gives ratios 1,5/8,13/32,103/256 and total 189978847362366308352; direct word check (3,2) gives 20
correctness.rationale: A distinct-window cyclic word is a labeled Euler circuit in the surviving graph, modulo cyclic shift, and its missing edges must be balanced. Three distinct balanced edges decompose into three loops, a loop and a two-cycle, or a three-cycle. For m≥2 all tails in every class are distinct: the double-symbol primitive three-cycle already has three different length-two phase prefixes. The orbit counts are binomial(q,3), q binomial(q,2), q(q−1), and 2 binomial(q,3). The undeleted shift has P^m=Π, hence the rooted cofactor is q^(q^m−n). The rank update for balanced deletion may be computed before showing connectivity because det(L_E+Π)=q^m τ_E also holds when the tree cofactor is zero. The inverse on zero-sum vectors is the finite geometric sum divided by q. Cell probabilities depend on suffix/prefix overlap, with extra matches only at one-letter overlap for the repeated-symbol period-three cycle. For a length-three cycle, multiplying the update determinant on the right by qI−R gives numerator det((q−1)I+xB_s) and denominator q³−1, where s=m mod 3. For three distinct symbols B_s=(I−R)R^s has trace (3,0,−3) by residue and sum of principal two-minors 3. For phase pattern (a,a,b), let U have the two nonzero entries U_01=U_10=1 in zero-based indices. Then B_s=(I−R)R^(s−1)[(I+U)R−qU]. Its trace by residue is (2−q,q,−2), and the principal two-minor sum is −q²−2q: for s=0 the three minors are −q²,−q,−q and R acts with determinant one on the zero-sum plane, leaving the product there invariant. Both matrices have determinant zero. Expanding in x and canceling q−1 yields exactly the two rows by residue in the frozen table. For d=2 the nonconstant shift eigenvalue −1 yields R₂ directly. All ratios are positive for q≥3 and x≤q⁻², so balance plus an in-tree gives strong connectivity. Fixing any surviving first edge in BEST counts each edge tour modulo rotation once; the distinct-window condition also excludes periodic words. At n=2 the uniform transition gives ratios 1−2/q and 1−3/q+3/q² on the two nonloop cycle types, but a loop at a two-cycle vertex changes one factorial twice; combining the four weights gives the separate claimed formula. All (n−1)-windows survive at least once because every vertex has positive degree, and distinct n-windows imply distinct longer windows, giving the stated maximal distinct-factor complexity. Independently enumerated deletion sets and exact cofactors for (q,n)=(3,4),(4,3) corroborated all four types; direct enumeration for (3,2) gave 20. The finite checks supplement the proof.
residual_risks: No all-parameter claim is based only on the finite checks. Alphabets remain labeled; reflections, symbol permutations and multiplicity-balanced restrictions are not imposed.

evidence: The inspected exact binary determinant has the same one-letter ambiguity for (a,a,b), so that mechanism is not claimed as an exclusive new technique. The order-three nonbinary tree ratios require both that correction at general q and a separate distinct-symbol period-three computation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Positive feasibility for a deleted set does not say how many circuits it leaves. Extending the binary method requires recomputing q-dependent minors, treating missing types absent over a binary alphabet, and combining their multiplicities and degrees, not replacing one numerical alphabet label in a known total.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the all-order, nonbinary exact necklace count at defect three with its type-dependent tree weights. The definition, existence-versus-Euler-count distinction and BEST/matrix-tree tools are prior. Some numerical entries are known. The closest binary exact result has analogous periodic overlap machinery, but lacks both the three-loop class and the distinct-symbol three-cycle class; the neighboring nonbinary defect-two result provides two-cycle machinery but neither period-three cofactor. The inspected sources do not subsume the full closed count.
residual_risks: A bounded search does not establish historical priority. The nonbinary three-defect formula, rather than individual known terms or the general cofactor machinery, is the scope of this pass.

value.rationale: This is a natural boundary case of exact near-power necklace enumeration, not a single hand-picked computed entry. The closed expression counts labeled rotation classes for every nonbinary alphabet and order at deficit three, and separates the structurally different missing cycles. Its residue dependence and the repeated-letter overlap correction explain why feasible deletion sets with the same number of edges can have different numbers of tours.
residual_risks: No general enumeration for larger deficits, all necklace lengths, or multiplicity-balanced necklaces is inferred.
